newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti - Foreign owners dismiss new issue.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti - Foreign owners dismiss new issue.

text.p: Foreign shareholders of ailing Italian hi-tech group Olivetti are "terrified" at the prospect of yet another rights issue, and do not support plans to sell off some of its stake in mobile phone group Omnitel.
Overseas stock holders would prefer a foreign group to take a strategic stake to help re-finance the troubled loss-making Italian group.
Mark Pignatelli, a representative of London-based Barings fund management, outlined these views to the industrial commission of Italy's parliamentary lower house.
He told the commission that foreign investors -- who hold a large stake in Olivetti -- were "terrified by the possibility of a new capital increase".
"Personally, I wouldn't support it, because it's a business that will not be profitable for five years," he said.

Olivetti's new chief executive Roberto Colaninno has said the group plans 1.2 trillion lire ($786 million) asset sales in the rest of 1996 and in 1997, and added that the group may need a capital increase at the end of 1997.
But Pignatelli said Olivetti should not be rushed to sell off key activities which its banks has requested in order to restructure its group debts.
"These will be needed by a purchaser of a strategic stake who is willing to pay a higher price than the market's current valuation," he said.

Olivetti wants to sell a 5.6 percent stake in Omnitel to German industrial group Mannesmann AG, a stake Olivetti only bought from Lehman Brothers at the time of last year's rights issue to bring its Omnitel stake up to 41.3 percent.

Olivetti launched its record 2.26 trillion lire rights issue late last year, which helped push the stake held by foreign shareholders up to 70 percent, but problems persisted at the group which has not made a profit since 1990.

Continuing losses from its personal computer business and a faltering performance in its key systems and services company and cash-absorbing new telecom businesses combined to keep the group in the red in the first half of 1996.
The chairman of the lower house industry commission Nerio Nesi, of the Communist Refoundation party, said he wanted to see parliamentary commission of enquiry to look into Olivetti. ($1=1,527 lire)
